title.narrative: IDP and Famine Response-Enhancing resilience and productive capacities for persons affected by the Sudan crises.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe project will provide integrated, lifesaving food security, livelihood, water, sanitation, and hygiene support to a population on the brink of starvation, with added vulnerabilities to water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH)-related morbidity.ltbrgtParticularlyltbrgtlt/pgtltolgtltligtThe Sudan war has caused massive displacement from the rest of Sudan into the central region of South Kordofan. lt/ligtltligtUnfortunately, the host community is unable to support the dignified settlement of the incoming internally displaced persons (IDPs) and returnees because the Host localities suffered a failed crop season in 2023 and have limited WASH service provision points and supplies. lt/ligtltligtConsequently, a significant proportion of the affected population, well above 50%, currently have livelihoods in integrated food security phase classification three (IPC3), IPC4, and IPC5. ltbrgtThe proposed project locality, Thobo County, is particularly severely affected by the food crisis. The entire population of 496,512 is at risk of famine (IPC5), with children under five at high risk of acute malnutrition.lt/ligtltligtAugmented with severe stress points in WASH, Health, and trauma, the Host, IDP, and returnees community is stretched thin. Over 500,000 vulnerable persons are now expected to share depleted resources in Food reserves, WASH, and Health facilities. lt/ligtltligtConflict sensitivity analyses project a high likelihood of resource-based conflict between Host communities and the IDP communities if immediate humanitarian response mechanisms are not put in place to arrest the imminent food crisis and ltbrgtWASH-associated morbidities in Thobo County.lt/ligtlt/olgtltpgtTherefore, the proposed IDP and Famine Response must explore the nexus between conflict, poverty, hunger, WASH-related diseases, and gender-based violence adapt complementary methodologies to the ongoing SHF and third-party funded projects in the region engage grassroots agricultural mechanisms with targeted input supplies and capacity-building, and WASH committees, and work towards building resilience in agricultural production, food security, nutrition, and WASH.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtUnder the famine response: ltbrgt1. The project will distribute farm inputs (Farm tools, Cereal, legumes, and Vegetable seeds) to women empowerment groups in Chani and Angolo Payam in Thobo County.ltbrgt2. The project will offer training and extension services on sustainable and climate-smart agriculture to the women groups engaged in agricultural production and,ltbrgt3. Conduct post-distribution monitoring to measure and report on the project's effectiveness and adapt the subsequent phase of programming accordingly based on lessons learned and the need for sustainability.ltbrgtUnder the WASH response:ltbrgt1. The project will repair boreholes for adequate water supply in Tabanya Payam/ or the resident Payam for the IDP community within Thobo County if relocations are to be effected in the rainy season.ltbrgt2. The project will construct communal sanitation facilities within the IDP community and,ltbrgt3. Form WASH committees and task members to own and conduct hygiene promotion alongside the project's hygiene promoters.ltbrgtThe project's implementation will utilize the existing partnerships between NCA and the Nuba Women's Union to allow for optimal local and ltbrgtgrassroots engagement of the affected persons, particularly women and girls. lt/pgtltpgtThe famine response will involve members of the women's union forming groups of 30 to 60 women. These women will then take up large-scale grain and vegetable production with support from the NCA, the local government structures, and all other relevant regional stakeholders.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe WASH response will involve WASH committees tasked with maintaining the WASH service points and extending necessary services to underserved, vulnerable persons.lt/pgt
